🐪 Good Wednesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 541 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) will hold a bipartisan briefing next week to discuss the "extraordinary dangers" posed by AI, Axios' Maria Curi has learned. Last month, Sanders called for pausing AI development.

  • Geoffrey Hinton, known as the "Godfather of AI," and Ajeya Cotra, one of the independent researchers who investigated the OpenAI-Hugging Face hacking incident, will attend the Senate briefing. Go deeper.
 
 
1 big thing: Meet the foldable iPhone Duo
 
Apple's iPhone Duo, the first foldable iPhone, was unveiled today at Apple Park in Cupertino, Calif. Photo: Jeff Chiu/AP

Apple debuted its first foldable iPhone today — along with the iPhone 18 Pro and updated Apple Watch and AirPods, Axios' Ina Fried reports.

  • It's the company's first major launch under CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

📱 The iPhone Duo features an inner display 80% larger than Apple's next-biggest iPhone, and it supports the Apple Pencil.

  • An under-display front-facing camera supports video chat, with two traditional cameras on the back of the phone.
Apple's iPhone Duo was the star of today's "Surprise and Shine" event. Photo: Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images

🤳 In demos, Apple showed how it redesigned its own apps to fit the new shape, while also highlighting how apps like Slack are using the added space.

  • Apple also touted techniques it used to make the Duo more durable than other foldable phones on the market.

What's next: The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 with 256GB of memory.

  • Pre-orders open Oct. 16, with shipments starting Oct. 23.

Go deeper.
 
 
2. ⚡️ Gas prices supercharge EV interest
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios

56% of drivers say high gas prices have raised their interest in electric cars, Axios' Jim Sergent reports from HERE Technologies and SBD Automotive's annual survey.

🔌 Charging availability is becoming less of a deterrent, too.

  • 47% of drivers say there's a good number of public chargers, up from 28% last year.

🤑 Yes, but: Higher purchase prices are holding back two in five would-be EV buyers, according to the survey.

  • Kelley Blue Book says Americans paid an average of $56,126 for a new EV in July.
  • That's $6,200 more than the typical car.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Waves crashing on seaside homes yesterday in Malibu, Calif. Photo: David Swanson/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🌊 More than 30 homes in Malibu, Calif., are under evacuation orders amid coastal flooding and erosion. Offshore storms have caused significant damage, including a massive sinkhole outside actor Nicolas Cage's $10.5 million beachfront home. Go deeper.
  2. 🧑‍⚖️ The lone juror who blocked Lindsay Clancy from being acquitted in Plymouth, Mass., insisted that he wouldn't find her not guilty by reason of insanity despite saying that he had reasonable doubt, the jury's foreperson said in an interview. Go deeper.
  3. 🏌️‍♂️ LIV Golf is asking a bankruptcy judge's permission to reject its player contracts, including lucrative deals with stars Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Phil Mickelson. More from Nathan Bomey.
 
 
4. 🕯️ D.C. marks 25 years since 9/11
 
A fragment of the airplane that crashed into the Pentagon on 9/11. Photo: Smithsonian Institution

The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History this week is highlighting about 40 objects tied to the World Trade Center, Pentagon and Flight 93 that are not currently on display, Axios D.C.'s Anna Spiegel reports.

  • The objects will be displayed on open tables rather than behind glass, for an unusually close look meant to "inspire respect and reflection."

⛑️ The Smithsonian's 9/11 collection has over 700 pieces, including plane and building fragments, first responders' gear, photographs and letters.

  • The museum will also screen the documentary "9/11: Stories in Fragments."
